Benchmark prediction models on identical folds

Source: R/pred.R
wgh_benchmark.Rd

Fits the late-adolescent height prediction study (Ho 2026, manuscript under review) model ladder (M0 baseline OLS through M8 random forest) separately by sex and evaluates every model on the same child-level cross-validation folds, so the comparison is fair. Missing feature values are imputed with training-fold medians. Book 1 Chapter 11's run_cv() is the teaching version of this function.

Usage

wgh_benchmark(
  cohort,
  models = paste0("M", 0:8),
  folds = wgh_opt("folds"),
  site_effect = c("fixed", "random"),
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

cohort

Output of wgh_prediction_cohort().

models

Models to run, from "M0" to "M8".

folds

Number of folds (default from the run mode), or "site" for leave-one-site-out geographic validation.

site_effect

"fixed" or "random".

seed

Random seed.

Value

An object of class wgh_benchmark with performance (cross- validated metrics by sex and model), apparent (in-sample metrics), predictions (out-of-fold predictions) and fits (full-data fits).

Details

By default site enters as a fixed effect, because a random intercept with only three sites is poorly estimated. site_effect = "random" gives the the late-adolescent height prediction study (Ho 2026, manuscript under review) specification.

Examples

# \donttest{
pc <- wgh_prediction_cohort(wgh_simulate(8000, seed = 4)$visits)
bm <- wgh_benchmark(pc, models = c("M0", "M1", "M5", "M8"), folds = 3)
bm
